Security policy

Source: SECURITY.md

crimlab is a statistical library: it reads the data a caller passes, and opens no network connection except in the documented readers of open data (odtab(), odls()). It implements no cryptography. It has not had an external security review.

Please report a vulnerability privately through GitHub’s “Report a vulnerability” button on this repository (Security tab, https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/security/advisories/new), not in a public issue. A reply comes within 7 days, and a fix and an advisory within 90 days. Fixed vulnerabilities are listed at https://github.com/rootcoder007/crimlab/security/advisories.

A crash, a hang or memory that grows without bound on input a caller could reasonably pass counts as a vulnerability here, in the R package, the command-line program and every binding. A wrong number is a bug: report it in the issue tracker.

Release signing key

Each release’s SHA256SUMS is signed with this SSH key (namespace file); the signature is the release file SHA256SUMS.sig.

ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIDCgdm/W6LtsPET14oTqb1lOFga52VG4HSJTtQHfLTFc

Fingerprint SHA256:o8zFxDLZk0Q4Cm00HWgHXqfD/rlI6TVLAI00OaAtrAk. To check a release, put the key in an allowed-signers file and verify the sums, then check the archive against them:

echo "crimlab ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIDCgdm/W6LtsPET14oTqb1lOFga52VG4HSJTtQHfLTFc" > allowed_signers
ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers -I crimlab -n file \
  -s SHA256SUMS.sig < SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS

install.sh and install.ps1 make the same check when the environment variable CRIMLAB_SIGNER holds that allowed-signers line (crimlab ssh-ed25519 ...); without it they check the archive against SHA256SUMS only.
